newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Assassins execute Taiwan magistrate, six others.
newsitem.headline: Assassins execute Taiwan magistrate, six others.

text.p: Gunmen burst into a Taiwan county magistrate's home, tied up nine people and shot each in the head on Thursday, methodically executing the official and six others in one of the island's most sensational crimes in memory.
The two surviving victims were in critical condition with no vital signs and were not expected to survive, officials said.
Taoyuan county magistrate Liu Pang-yu, a member of Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party, died in hospital seven hours after the morning shooting, a Taoyuan provincial hospital spokesman said.
Two Taoyuan county council members were among the dead.
"We are not optimistic about the surviving two, who are in very critical condition," the spokesman said by telephone.
Taoyuan police said two gunmen burst into Liu's home, bound the hands of Liu and eight others and systematically shot each in the head at close range. Five died at the scene.
Police declined to comment on any possible motives for one of the most horrific crimes to hit Taiwan in years.

The assassination rekindled memories of the February 28, 1980, killing of the mother and daughters of an imprisoned Taiwan independence advocate in their home in a politically charged case that remains unsolved.

The Justice Ministry in August launched a crackdown on scores of criminal gangs that Justice Minister Liao Cheng-hao said had infiltrated Taiwan's business and political circles and even Parliament, triggering fears of gang reprisals.
Police said magistrate Liu's killers worked swiftly in what appeared to be a premeditated crime.
"The method of the shooting shows that they wanted them die at once. It happened in just about 10 minutes," a police spokesman said from Taoyuan.

Investigators found a getaway car abandoned by the gunmen in the mountains, and police were mounting a massive search for the killers, he said. Taiwan's air and seaports were ordered to conduct stepped up checks of all departing passengers.
The state-run Central News Agency, without citing a source, said the killings could involve a property development case.
Investigators would not rule out a link to Taiwan's rough and tumble politics, newspapers said, while state radio said the killers could have underworld connections.
Aside from magistrate Liu, 54, and the two council members, police said the victims included Liu's cousin and several staff members -- security guards, a driver, a secretary and a maid.
President Lee Teng-hui's office issued a statement of regret and called for speedy police work.
"President Lee is extremely shocked," it said. "He has ordered related government agencies to solve the case as soon as possible."
Evening newspapers splashed grisly pictures of the scene on their front pages and condemned the brazen show of brutality at the home of a senior government official.
"This is a common scene in movies," the China Times Express said in an editorial. "Unfortunately this is no longer just a movie plot but the real situation in Taiwan."
The United Evening News appealed for public faith and police vigilance in an editorial headlined, "Taiwan has become Sicily".
"Don't let the people lose confidence in the government's ability to crack down on crimes," the newspaper said.
